what_it_does: This paper optimizes the training of deep learning recommendation models (DLRMs) across multiple graphics processors. The embedding layer in DLRMs—which maps user and item identifiers to learned vectors—creates an aggregation bottleneck where each GPU gathers its embedding results and reduces them across all GPUs. Unlike traditional collective operations that follow fixed patterns, this aggregation depends on the actual input data (which items the batch contains), making it resistant to existing in-network acceleration schemes. The paper introduces specialized network switch hardware that identifies when the same embedding is requested from multiple GPUs and performs the aggregation directly in the network rather than routing all data back to the host processor.
